issues.description: Attribute mismatch for Course.ratings: the problem statement (problem_statement.md) and the template (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift) specify Course.ratings as [Int], but the solution (Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift in the solution repository) declares Course.ratings as [Double] and its initializer accepts [Double]. This contradicts the exercise description and the starter code and causes a real build/confusion problem because the solution's addRating(stars:) appends Int values and getAverageRating() treats ratings as integers — appending Int to a [Double] array or summing mismatched types would produce compilation errors and will confuse students about the expected rating element type.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the ratings element type consistent across all artifacts. Recommended: change the solution to use ratings: [Int] (to match the problem statement and template). Concretely update solution Sources/DeveloperLib/Course.swift: change the property to var ratings: [Int], change the initializer parameter to ratings: [Int], ensure addRating(stars:) appends Int values, and implement getAverageRating() by summing Ints and returning Double(sum) / Double(count) with zero-division handling. Alternatively, if Double ratings are intended, update the problem statement and the template to document ratings as [Double] and adjust all method implementations and signatures accordingly. The first option (use Int) preserves the original exercise text and is preferred.
